title: Batavia Detention Infrastructure
description: ICE ERO requires a temporary detention structure to safely house up to 100 detainees of all security levels. The structure shall be located and placed in the area proposed by the contractor within the confines of the existing detention facility. The structures and services shall conform to the most current version of the Performance-Based National Detention Standards 2011, with 2016 revisions. The structure must also meet all American Correctional Association requirements and all applicable DHS/ICE policies and procedures. The contractor shall provide all necessary systems, equipment, supplies, labor, infrastructure, and support of sufficient size and scope to safely house and service a population of up to 100 detainees. The contractor shall meet all requirements outlined in the applicable standards and the performance work statement. The contractor shall provide and install self-sustaining utilities. The temporary structures shall not tie into existing water, sewage, electrical, or other facility infrastructure unless expressly authorized by the Government. The contractor shall provide turnkey housing and medical structures, including flooring and other features necessary to support up to 100 detainees using double-bunk configurations. The contractor shall furnish all installation support and equipment related to the temporary detention structure and integrated medical structure. The contractor is responsible for installation oversight, management, supervision, trained personnel, materials, supplies, licenses, permits, and all other resources necessary for the project. The contractor shall purchase ICE Health Service Corps furniture, fixtures, and medical equipment as a one-time purchase, maintain such items as required, and provide an initial order of medical office and medical supplies, with ongoing purchases as needed.

title: Rental of Secure Storage Facility for ICE/ERO/Buffalo Field Office
description: The U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS), Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), Enforcement and Removal Operations (ERO) Buffalo Field Office requires secure storage for its Special Response Team (SRT) assets. These assets are currently held at the secure storage facility operated by the Town of Lancaster, NY at the Lancaster Police Department (LPD) facility located at 525 Pavement Road in Lancaster, NY. Approximately $500,000.00 of agency assets are stored at this facility. Storing these agency assets at any other secure storage facility in the Buffalo, NY metro area would present a significant logistical challenge with respect to the coordination of the pick-up/drop-off of assets at the two ICE/ERO facilities (Buffalo Field Office in downtown Buffalo and the Buffalo Federal Detention Facility (BFDF) in Batavia, NY) located within the ICE/ERO Buffalo Area of Responsibility (AoR) . It is therefore necessary to continue to utilize the LPD secure facility to store all SRT assets in a central location between the ICE/ERO Buffalo and Batavia facilities. The LPD facility is within close proximity (five miles) of the Buffalo-Niagara International Airport. Proximity to the airport is required because of the many times SRT is deployed to assist ERO flights at the airport. Based upon the Market Research conducted by ICE/ERO/Buffalo Field Office, and a consideration of available commercial sources and law enforcement organizations within 10 minutes (or around 5 miles) of the Buffalo-Niagara International Airport, the Contracting Officer has determined the Lancaster Police Department (LPD) is the only source that can meet the specifications stated in the Statement of Work (SOW) to provide secure storage for ICE/ERO/Buffalo Field Office SRT assets.

title: Limited Competition Justification and Award Notice Outbound Shipments
description: The purpose of this notice is to comply with posting requirement, FAR Part 5 and Subpart 6.301. Competition was restricted to a limited number of vendors capable of meeting current operational requirements, including the ability to ship via alternative routes. This restriction is necessary due to constraints imposed by ongoing regional instability, which has rendered standard shipping routes unreliable or unavailable. Limiting competition to qualified vendors ensures continuity of outbound shipping services under current conditions. The security situation in the region remains fluid and subject to sudden escalation. Recurring, rapid changes in regional security conditions are affecting carrier availability, shipping routes, transit times, insurance requirements, and overall logistics reliability with little advance notice. Shipping activity through the Strait of Hormuz and other regional transportation corridors is unreliable and dangerous, with a result of limited bookings available from limited shippers In accordance with FAR 12.201-1(c)(2)(ii), simplified acquisition procedures, quotations were solicited from three vendors determined capable of meeting the Government�s requirements under current operational conditions. Three quotations were received and evaluated based on technical capability, compliance with the required scope of services, demonstrated ability to meet urgent logistical and delivery requirements, relevant past performance, and price reasonableness. The selected contractor was determined to represent the lowest-priced technically acceptable quotation $26,206 USD and demonstrated the capability to successfully perform the required services within the required timeframe and operational constraints. The contractor also demonstrated a strong record of relevant past performance supporting U.S. Embassy Kuwait requirements, including reliable and quality performance under similar operational conditions. Award to this contractor will support Shipping in maintaining uninterrupted mission operations and accomplishing mission requirements
